items.title: Early government modelling shows how long fuel stockpile lasts if imports slow
items.description: Diesel stocks would last about six months if Australia's imports dropped by 20 per cent, according to modelling compiled for the federal government early in the Middle East war.

items.title: Petrol stations tried to 'shape' the market – now it's shaping them
items.description: Petrol stations in our biggest cities hiked prices ahead of global oil prices, but experts say their profit margins are now much slimmer.

items.title: Surcharges on debit and credit cards to go from October
items.description: The removal of surcharges on debit and credit cards is one of the sweeping reforms from the Reserve Bank.

items.title: Fair Work Commission abolishes junior pay rates for young adults
items.description: The Fair Work Commission has issued its decision to abolish junior pay rates for young adult employees in the retail, fast food, and pharmacy sectors while maintaining them for minors.

items.title: Jackie 'O' Henderson files legal action against ARN Media
items.description: Former Sydney radio broadcaster Jackie "O" Henderson has filed legal action against employer ARN Media, following the collapse of the hit Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: A minute before Trump's wild Iran claim, oil traders made 'abnormal' moves
items.description: Global stock markets, which for the past month have been remarkably restrained as the Middle East crisis unfolded, have begun to wobble.

items.title: Live: Spain closes airspace to US planes involved in Middle East war
items.description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt says US President Donald Trump is interested in getting Arab countries to pay for the war in the Middle East. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Wong reiterates Australia will not provide boots on ground in Iran war
items.description: Foreign Minister Penny Wong says Australia has been clear that it will not provide troops on the ground for an operation against Iran. Follow live.

items.title: The day Porepunkah went quiet and learned Dezi Freeman was dead
items.description: Seven months after a gunman killed two police officers on its streets, the tiny town woke to news that Dezi Freeman was dead.

items.title: Iran's 'safe passage' signals a new global divide
items.description: China is now the world's largest crude oil importer, and Iran — though a discounted and often opaque supplier — remains a consistent part of that supply mix.

items.title: How one man's stolen identity was used to run a cult
items.description: In mid-2009 British citizen Simon Kadwill-Kelly was catching a ferry returning from France. Within minutes of trying to board he found out his identity had been stolen.

items.title: 'I'm sick of it': One in two Australians priced out of healthcare system
items.description: One in two Australians missed out on health care they needed last year mainly because they could not afford it, according to a new report by the peak healthcare consumers group.

items.title: Five illegal fishing vessels burned at sea amid ABF crackdown
items.description: The Australian Border Force launched a crackdown on illegal fishing in the state's north last month, with 19 boats intercepted since the beginning of the year.

items.title: Céline Dion to perform again after years-long health-related hiatus
items.description: The My Heart Will Go On singer disclosed in 2022 that she had a rare neurological disease, indefinitely cancelling her shows.

items.title: How to tell if you have insufficient insurance for your home and contents
items.description: If your home is underinsured, it means your insurance policy won't fully cover the cost of rebuilding, repairing or replacing it.

items.title: Transphobia nearly killed Kaz. Now he just wants to be 'me'
items.description: This WA teenager was depressed, ill and missing out on school. He says it was part of the toll transphobia took on him.

items.title: 'A succulent Chinese meal?': These are the 2026 Sounds of Australia
items.description: A variety of iconic Australian recordings are added to the Sounds of Australia collection, as part of an annual update by the National Film and Sound Archive.

items.title: Supermarket chicken could get cheaper due to grain breakthrough
items.description: Australian researchers develop a high-protein sorghum variety, hoping to replace expensive livestock feed with systems that could lead to cheaper meat and eggs.

items.title: Passengers fear further V/Line overcrowding as free travel begins
items.description: Commuters say they are worried overcrowding on V/Line train services could worsen as free travel begins for Victorians to ease the pain of the fuel crisis.

items.title: Anonymous $200,000 donation helps free dinner service as demand doubles
items.description: The cash donation alongside a free van will help the charity continue to feed people in need and allow it to expand its service.

items.title: Businesses report increase in abuse from customers as fuel crisis worsens
items.description: From pile-on comments on social media to roadside slurs, local businesses are reminding their communities to "be kind to the little guy" amid the fuel crisis.

items.title: Live: Consumer confidence hits 53-year low, ASX and AUD down
items.description: Consumer confidence across Australia has hit its worst level since tracking began in 1973, according to the latest ANZ-Roy Morgan survey. Follow the day's events on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Black-robed lawyers and 'killer' beef at Kimberley court
items.description: It was a court hearing unlike any other, complete with country music, "killer" beef, and gaggles of kids and dogs dashing between the black-clad lawyers.

items.title: Five social media companies investigated over response to teen ban
items.description: Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube are being investigated for potential noncompliance with the ban, almost four months after the laws came into force.

items.title: Man charged over seaside pub shooting, armed robbery and carjacking
items.description: Police have arrested and charged 41-year-old Deon Rodney Mason over the shooting and alleged armed robbery at a pub on the NSW far south coast.
